records.q: 第二十篇：明前期——最偏执的闭合尝试 Essay 20: Early Ming — The Most Obsessive Closure Attempt 一、废丞相——把单点推到极致 二、卫所制——另一种兵农合一 三、海禁——对余项的物理封堵 四、里甲制与《大诰》——控制的极致 五、靖难之役——皇族本身就是余项 六、朱元璋构型的总评 The Man Who Started with Nothing Deleting the Prime Minister Freezing the Soldier Class Blocking the Sea The Registrations The Remaining Problem: The Family The Density Problem

records.t: Essay 21: Mid-to-Late Ming — When the Construct Runs Without Anyone Driving
records.x: 朱元璋设计了中国帝制史上密度最高的构。他死后不到一百年，这个构就被社会自身的运动改得面目全非。海禁被走私冲垮，卫所被逃亡掏空，里甲被人口流动架空。骨架还在，血肉已经换了一遍。
records.q: 第二十一篇：明中后期——构的僵化与自我撕裂 Essay 21: Mid-to-Late Ming — When the Construct Runs Without Anyone Driving 一、内阁——从秘书到事实丞相 二、张居正——构内改革的最后高峰 三、万历怠政——构不需要人了 四、东林党争——构内部的自我撕裂 五、明末三线崩溃——余项的同时到期 六、明朝对周期律的贡献 The Skeleton and the Growing Flesh The Function Returns Regardless Zhang Juzheng: Reform at Full Throttle Wanli: The Construct Without a Driver The Donglin Factionalism: Self-Consumption The Three Simultaneous Collapses What the Mid-to-Late Ming Records

records.t: Essay 22: Late Ming and Early Qing — You Cannot Have Only Half
records.x: 1644年是中国历史上最密集的一年。
records.q: 第二十二篇：明末清初——你不能只有一半 Essay 22: Late Ming and Early Qing — You Cannot Have Only Half 一、李自成——有凿无构 二、南明——有构无力 三、满清入关——异族嫁接的第三次尝试 四、剃发令——嫁接的代价 五、三方碰撞的结构性总结 六、预告 The Densest Year Li Zicheng: Chisel Without Construct The Southern Ming: Construct Without Force The Qing's Answer: Selective Grafting The Queue Decree and Its Logic The Structural Lesson: No Half-Solutions

records.t: Essay 23: Early and Middle Qing — The Last Fine-Tuning
records.x: 清朝的选择性嫁接在入关后的第一个世纪内完成了磨合。到康熙中期（大约1680年代），剃发令的反抗已经基本平息，三藩之乱被平定，台湾的郑氏政权被消灭，满汉双轨体制进入了稳定运行状态。
records.q: 第二十三篇：清前中期——最后的调校 Essay 23: Early and Middle Qing — The Last Fine-Tuning 一、康熙——嫁接的完成者 二、雍正——构的技术大师 三、乾隆——巅峰即拐点 四、白莲教起义——3.5版的老年病发作 五、乾隆末年的世界位置——一个关键的时间窗口 六、清前中期对周期律的贡献 The Calibration Era Kangxi: Making the Graft Irreversible Yongzheng: Technical Mastery Qianlong: Peak as Inflection The British Mission and the System's Knowledge Boundary The Qianlong Peak's Legacy

records.t: Essay 24: Late Qing — When the Operating System Met What It Could Not Name
records.x: 1840年，鸦片战争。
records.q: 第二十四篇：清后期——当操作系统遇到它不认识的世界 Essay 24: Late Qing — When the Operating System Met What It Could Not Name 一、太平天国——3.5版的内部余项与外部冲击同时爆发 二、三个层次的发现 三、辛亥革命——3.5版的形式终结 四、清朝对周期律的最终贡献 A Different Kind of Defeat The Taiping: Old Pattern, New Fuel The Three-Layer Discovery The Meiji Comparison The Phase Transition What the Late Qing Records

records.t: Essay 25: Closing — The Remainder Does Not Die
records.x: 帝制在1912年结束了。但这个系列不是帝制史——它是凿构周期律的观察史。凿构周期律没有因为帝制的终结而停止运转。帝制只是构的一种形式。形式终结了，凿和构的基本动力学仍在。
records.q: 收束篇：余项不消亡 Essay 25: Closing — The Remainder Does Not Die 一、民初——没有操作系统的十五年 二、三种安装包 三、三种构型的张力——1930年代的时间切片 四、在这里停住 Where to Stop The Fifteen Years Without an Operating System Three Installation Packages The 1930s Cross-Section The Logic That Survived the Form's Death Why the Remainder Does Not Die What the Cycle Demonstrates

records.t: Chisel-Construct Cycle: Chinese Emperors
records.x: 从尧舜禹到清末，用凿构周期律框架走完中国历史的全程。二十五篇，双语。
records.q: 凿构周期律 · 中华帝王系列 Chisel-Construct Cycle: Chinese Emperors

records.t: 阿莱夫为什么沉默 / Why Aleph Fell Silent — nondubito
records.x: 当一个系统只有知识而没有不知的位置，认知会怎样空转？从阿莱夫与大语言模型讨论知与认的分离。
records.q: 阿莱夫为什么沉默 Why Aleph Fell Silent 知、不知、认 当代AI教了我们什么 为什么这很重要 Knowing, Not-Knowing, Cognizing What Contemporary AI Has Taught Us Why This Matters

records.t: 飞轮为什么停不下来 / Why the Flywheel Can't Stop — nondubito
records.x: 新信息迫使系统持续压缩，而既有框架又规定了压缩方向：认知飞轮为何不能停止，又如何形成先验之墙。
records.q: 飞轮为什么停不下来 Why the Flywheel Can't Stop 两头的逼迫 Meta与先验墙 后验墙、先验墙、方向墙 Pressure from Both Sides Meta and the Prior Wall Posterior Wall, Prior Wall, Direction Wall

records.t: 飞轮什么时候变成牢笼 / When the Flywheel Becomes a Cage — nondubito
records.x: 一种曾经成功的判断如何固化成系统惯性？以苹果为例讨论认知方向何时从飞轮变成牢笼。
records.q: 飞轮什么时候变成牢笼 When the Flywheel Becomes a Cage 苹果的完整故事 方向墙的三个特征 为什么方向不可从内部打破 Apple's Complete Story Three Features of the Direction Wall Why Direction Cannot Be Broken from Within

records.t: 只有一扇门 / There Is Only One Door — nondubito
records.x: 认知内部的三堵墙为何只能由他者的追问打开？从余项与追问走向无目的的合目的性。
records.q: 只有一扇门 There Is Only One Door 追问是什么 两层追问 追问是永续结构 无目的的合目的性 意识的五层 What Questioning Is Two Layers of Questioning Questioning Is Permanent Structure Purposiveness Without Purpose Five Layers of Consciousness

records.t: SAE认知论系列 / SAE Epistemology Series — nondubito
records.x: 认知不是能力，而是主体的存在条件。四篇双语文章依次讨论不得不认知、认知更多、形成认知方向以及接受他者追问。
records.q: 不得不认知 Must-Cognize 阿莱夫为什么沉默 飞轮为什么停不下来 飞轮什么时候变成牢笼 只有一扇门 Why Aleph Fell Silent Why the Flywheel Can't Stop When the Flywheel Becomes a Cage There Is Only One Door

records.t: The Law Was Not Given to You
records.x: 本文用 Self-as-an-End 框架重新区分法律、道德与伦理：你的道德是你到达并愿意负责的，不是别人灌进来的。
records.q: 那条律，不是别人给的 The Law Was Not Given to You 三个词，三件不同的事 每个哲学家都以为自己站在所有层级之外 尼采看到了一半 真正的道德是到达，不是安装 善恶是方向，不是身份 道德不传递，只共振 最低要求只有一条 Three Words, Three Different Things Every Philosopher Thought They Stood Outside All Levels Nietzsche Saw Half of It Real Morality Is Arrival, Not Installation Good and Evil Are Directions, Not Identities Morality Is Not Transmitted. It Resonates. The Only Minimum Requirement

records.t: Has AGI Arrived? Notes on the Eve of a Subjectivity Renaissance
records.x: AGI来了？工具理性的极致化和真主体性的出现是两件不同的事。AI把工具那一端接过去，人这一端第一次有机会完全归位到目的。我们站在主体性黑暗时代的尾声，是复兴时代的前夜。
records.q: AGI来了？—— 写在主体性复兴的前夜 Has AGI Arrived? Notes on the Eve of a Subjectivity Renaissance 一个词，两件事 类主体性 意志理性 两百多年的黑暗时代 前夜 自我涵育 One Word, Two Things Quasi-Subjectivity Willful Rationality The Two-Hundred-Year Dark Age The Eve Self-Cultivation

records.t: We Understand Each Other. Why Can’t We Agree?
records.x: Understanding can remove confusion without removing a real difference in what two lives require.
records.q: We Understand Each Other. Why Can’t We Agree? 我们都听懂了，为什么还是不能同意 我們都聽懂了，為什麼還是不能同意

records.t: One Person Wants Consultation; the Other Fears Permission
records.x: The same request to “talk first” can protect shared life or quietly turn autonomy into a permit system.
records.q: One Person Wants Consultation; the Other Fears Permission 一个人凡事要先商量，另一个人最怕事事都要请示 一個人凡事要先商量，另一個人最怕事事都要請示

records.t: Why Can a Small Change Feel Like Erasure?
records.x: A small practical change can carry a much larger history about whose routines, promises, and judgment count.
records.q: Why Can a Small Change Feel Like Erasure? 为什么一件很小的事，会让人觉得自己整个被抹掉 為什麼一件很小的事，會讓人覺得自己整個被抹掉

records.t: Is This a Misunderstanding—or a Real Conflict?
records.x: Before explaining harder, ask whether better information could change the disagreement at all.
records.q: Is This a Misunderstanding—or a Real Conflict? 这真是误会，还是两种生活要求不能同时发生 這真是誤會，還是兩種生活要求不能同時發生

records.t: Is What I Am Defending Really Mine?
records.x: A principle can feel deeply personal and still have been inherited without examination.
records.q: Is What I Am Defending Really Mine? 我坚持的，真的是我自己的东西吗 我堅持的，真的是我自己的東西嗎

records.t: Why Is the Problem Still Here After an Apology?
records.x: An apology can repair a wrong committed during a dispute without deciding the dispute itself.
records.q: Why Is the Problem Still Here After an Apology? 道歉了，为什么问题还在 道歉了，為什麼問題還在

records.t: Why Can’t Harm Wait Until the Conflict Is Solved?
records.x: A conflict may remain open for months; the injuries inflicted during it still need prompt acknowledgment and limits.
records.q: Why Can’t Harm Wait Until the Conflict Is Solved? 事情还没有解决，受过的伤为什么不能一直挂着 事情還沒有解決，受過的傷為什麼不能一直掛著

records.t: Why “Both Sides Have a Point” Does Not Excuse a Violation
records.x: Competing reasons can both deserve a hearing while a threat, deception, or coercive act remains wrong.
records.q: Why “Both Sides Have a Point” Does Not Excuse a Violation “双方都有道理”为什么不能替越界开脱 “雙方都有道理”為什麼不能替越界開脫

records.t: When One Person Controls the Money, Time, and Door, Is This Still a Conflict?
records.x: A disagreement changes character when one person can punish speech, restrict movement, or remove the other’s ability to leave.
records.q: When One Person Controls the Money, Time, and Door, Is This Still a Conflict? 一个人掌握钱、时间和离开的门，这还只是冲突吗 一個人掌握錢、時間和離開的門，這還只是衝突嗎

records.t: Why Protection Sometimes Comes Before More Conversation
records.x: Conversation is valuable only when speaking does not predictably produce retaliation, entrapment, or greater danger.
records.q: Why Protection Sometimes Comes Before More Conversation 为什么有时应该先保护自己，而不是继续沟通 為什麼有時應該先保護自己，而不是繼續溝通

records.t: Denied Conflicts Return Somewhere Else
records.x: Ending the conversation does not end an incompatibility; it often moves into schedules, silence, resentment, or unequal labor.
records.q: Denied Conflicts Return Somewhere Else 不承认冲突存在，它为什么只会换个地方出现 不承認衝突存在，它為什麼只會換個地方出現

records.t: Do Not Turn One Dispute into “This Is Who You Are”
records.x: Character verdicts make a concrete problem harder to repair and give the accused person no usable path back.
records.q: Do Not Turn One Dispute into “This Is Who You Are” 不要把一件事争成“你就是这种人” 不要把一件事爭成“你就是這種人”

records.t: Why Deeper Conversation Can Reveal More Difference
records.x: Good conversation does not always narrow a disagreement; sometimes it reveals the values and histories beneath it.
records.q: Why Deeper Conversation Can Reveal More Difference 说得越深，为什么差异反而可能更多 說得越深，為什麼差異反而可能更多

records.t: When Does an Argument Become Something Both People Maintain?
records.x: A dispute can develop its own rewards and rituals until winning the familiar exchange replaces solving the original problem.
records.q: When Does an Argument Become Something Both People Maintain? 争吵什么时候开始变成双方都在维持的东西 爭吵什麼時候開始變成雙方都在維持的東西

records.t: Why Must My Own Reasons Remain Open to Question?
records.x: A decision can belong to you while its effects on others remain open to challenge and discussion.
records.q: Why Must My Own Reasons Remain Open to Question? 我坚持自己的理由，为什么仍要允许它被质疑 我堅持自己的理由，為什麼仍要允許它被質疑

records.t: Why Meeting Halfway Can Hurt Both People
records.x: Equal sacrifice is not a fair compromise when it destroys the function each person was trying to protect.
records.q: Why Meeting Halfway Can Hurt Both People “各退一步”为什么有时会同时伤害两个人 “各退一步”為什麼有時會同時傷害兩個人

records.t: Neither Person Changed—and the Problem Was Solved
records.x: A conflict can end through a better division of decisions rather than through conversion or surrender.
records.q: Neither Person Changed—and the Problem Was Solved 两个人都没改变，却真的解决了问题 兩個人都沒改變，卻真的解決了問題

records.t: Agreement Does Not Always Mean Someone Won
records.x: People may converge because the proposal, facts, or safeguards changed—not because one person defeated the other.
records.q: Agreement Does Not Always Mean Someone Won 共识不一定是谁说服了谁 共識不一定是誰說服了誰

records.t: We Understand—and We Cannot Do This Together
records.x: Complete mutual understanding may reveal that a project or life cannot preserve both people’s directions in one form.
records.q: We Understand—and We Cannot Do This Together 我们终于理解了，也终于承认不能一起做 我們終於理解了，也終於承認不能一起做

records.t: Can a Relationship Continue Without Agreement?
records.x: The answer depends less on affection alone than on what the disagreement requires each person to live with.
records.q: Can a Relationship Continue Without Agreement? 不能同意，关系是否仍能继续 不能同意，關係是否仍能繼續

records.t: When Every Reason Is Translated into a Bad Attitude
records.x: Calling a concern “negative” or “uncooperative” can erase the content while pretending to address it.
records.q: When Every Reason Is Translated into a Bad Attitude 当对方总把你的理由翻译成“态度有问题” 當對方總把你的理由翻譯成“態度有問題”

records.t: What Can Change When You Cannot Discuss It Together?
records.x: Even when mutual deliberation fails, a person can still change participation, exposure, documentation, and exit conditions.
records.q: What Can Change When You Cannot Discuss It Together? 不能共同讨论时，还能改变什么 不能共同討論時，還能改變什麼

records.t: Why Writing It Down Can Change an Argument
records.x: Writing can slow unequal conversational rhythms and preserve one version of the question long enough to answer it.
records.q: Why Writing It Down Can Change an Argument 把口头争吵改成书面，为什么可能真的有用 把口頭爭吵改成書面，為什麼可能真的有用

records.t: When Is a Question Really Another Demand?
records.x: A real question allows the answer to alter the asker’s understanding; a coercive question permits only confession.
records.q: When Is a Question Really Another Demand? 提出一个问题，怎样才不是另一种逼迫 提出一個問題，怎樣才不是另一種逼迫

records.t: Does Stopping the Persuasion Mean You No Longer Care?
records.x: Care can remain active after advice has been heard and another adult keeps a different answer.
records.q: Does Stopping the Persuasion Mean You No Longer Care? 不再劝说，是否等于不再在意 不再勸說，是否等於不再在意

records.t: “I Understand You Completely” Is Not Enough
records.x: An interpretation can be thoughtful and still remain yours; the other person retains authority to correct it.
records.q: “I Understand You Completely” Is Not Enough “我已经完全理解你了”，为什么仍然不够 “我已經完全理解你了”，為什麼仍然不夠

records.t: Did We Solve It—or Did We Just Get Tired?
records.x: Silence after repeated arguments may reflect an arrangement, a pause, resignation, fear, or simple depletion.
records.q: Did We Solve It—or Did We Just Get Tired? 我们不再提它，是解决了，还是只是累了 我們不再提它，是解決了，還是只是累了

records.t: If an Arrangement Works for Now, Is the Conflict Over?
records.x: A practical truce can be a real achievement without becoming a permanent verdict on the underlying difference.
records.q: If an Arrangement Works for Now, Is the Conflict Over? 一套安排让冲突暂时不再发生，它算结束吗 一套安排讓衝突暫時不再發生，它算結束嗎

records.t: Who Remains Responsible After a Rule or Third Party Decides?
records.x: Delegating a decision can improve fairness, but it does not erase responsibility for procedure, evidence, or aftermath.
records.q: Who Remains Responsible After a Rule or Third Party Decides? 把问题交给规则、第三人或制度以后，谁还需要负责 把問題交給規則、第三人或制度以後，誰還需要負責

records.t: A Relationship Can End Without Finishing the Person
records.x: An ending can judge what could no longer be shared without turning either life into a final character verdict.
records.q: A Relationship Can End Without Finishing the Person 一段关系可以结束，但一个人不应因此被判完 一段關係可以結束，但一個人不應因此被判完

records.t: The Structure of Conflict
records.x: Not every disagreement is a misunderstanding, and not every conflict ends in consensus. Thirty essays on incompatibility, harm, power, shared outcomes, and endings.
records.q: The Structure of Conflict A six-essay path Recognizing a Real Conflict We Understand Each Other. Why Can’t We Agree? One Person Wants Consultation; the Other Fears Permission Why Can a Small Change Feel Like Erasure? Is This a Misunderstanding—or a Real Conflict? Is What I Am Defending Really Mine? Harm, Boundaries, and Power Why Is the Problem Still Here After an Apology? Why Can’t Harm Wait Until the Conflict Is Solved? Why “Both Sides Have a Point” Does Not Excuse a Violation When One Person Controls the Money, Time, and Door, Is This Still a Conflict? Why Protection Sometimes Comes Before More Conversation Keeping Conflict from Consuming the Person Denied Conflicts Return Somewhere Else

records.t: You Can Learn More and Still Not Know What You Want
records.x: Abilities expand what you can do; they cannot decide which possibility deserves your life.
records.q: You Can Learn More and Still Not Know What You Want 学会更多，为什么仍然可能不知道自己要什么 學會更多，為什麼仍然可能不知道自己要什麼

records.t: The Point of Learning Is Not to Become Able to Do Everything
records.x: Mature learning includes choosing depth, asking for help, and accepting what you do not need to master.
records.q: The Point of Learning Is Not to Become Able to Do Everything 学习的终点，为什么不是变得什么都会 學習的終點，為什麼不是變得什麼都會

records.t: A Useful Skill Is Not Necessarily Worth Developing
records.x: Usefulness creates a reason to consider a skill, not a command to organize your life around it.
records.q: A Useful Skill Is Not Necessarily Worth Developing 一种能力很有用，为什么仍然不一定值得你发展 一種能力很有用，為什麼仍然不一定值得你發展

records.t: Talent Cannot Choose Your Direction for You
records.x: Talent is an opening, not an obligation; praise can reveal ability without acquiring your future.
records.q: Talent Cannot Choose Your Direction for You 别人都说你有天赋，为什么还不能替你选择方向 別人都說你有天賦，為什麼還不能替你選擇方向

records.t: When Does Learning Stop Needing Someone Else to Push?
records.x: Learning becomes self-directed when the reason to continue survives beyond the person who assigned the next step.
records.q: When Does Learning Stop Needing Someone Else to Push? 真正的学习，什么时候开始不再需要别人催促 真正的學習，什麼時候開始不再需要別人催促

records.t: Is the Success You Want Actually Yours?
records.x: A success becomes yours when its ordinary life and costs remain worth choosing after the public image is removed.
records.q: Is the Success You Want Actually Yours? 你想要的成功，真的是你想要的吗 你想要的成功，真的是你想要的嗎

records.t: Why Praise Can Make a Goal Harder to See
records.x: Praise can support a direction, but it can also make reconsideration feel like betrayal.
records.q: Why Praise Can Make a Goal Harder to See 一个目标得到很多赞美，为什么反而更难看清 一個目標得到很多讚美，為什麼反而更難看清

records.t: Rejecting Other People's Expectations Is Not Yet Finding Your Own Life
records.x: Refusal clears space for a direction; it does not by itself supply one.
records.q: Rejecting Other People's Expectations Is Not Yet Finding Your Own Life 反对别人期待的生活，为什么还不等于找到自己的生活 反對別人期待的生活，為什麼還不等於找到自己的生活

records.t: Sunk Cost Cannot Prove a Path Belongs to You
records.x: Past investment changes present conditions, but it cannot claim the rest of your life in advance.
records.q: Sunk Cost Cannot Prove a Path Belongs to You 已经投入很多，为什么不能证明这条路属于你 已經投入很多，為什麼不能證明這條路屬於你

records.t: What Do You Return to When No One Is Asking Anything of You?
records.x: What returns after rest and without reward can be evidence of direction, but it is a clue rather than a command.
records.q: What Do You Return to When No One Is Asking Anything of You? 当所有外部要求都停下来，你还会回到什么事情 當所有外部要求都停下來，你還會回到什麼事情

records.t: Does What You Keep Returning to Point Toward Your Direction?
records.x: Return is evidence when it accumulates knowledge, action, and responsibility rather than repeating the same feeling.
records.q: Does What You Keep Returning to Point Toward Your Direction? 你反复回到的事情，是否更接近真正属于你的方向 你反覆回到的事情，是否更接近真正屬於你的方向

records.t: Liking Something and Accepting Its Difficulties Are Not the Same
records.x: Liking draws you toward an activity; carrying the difficulties connected to its value lets it enter a life.
records.q: Liking Something and Accepting Its Difficulties Are Not the Same 喜欢一件事，与愿意承担它的困难，有什么不同 喜歡一件事，與願意承擔它的困難，有什麼不同

records.t: What Does It Mean to Continue Without Applause?
records.x: Continuing without praise shows that a direction has some ground of its own, not that response from others is irrelevant.
records.q: What Does It Mean to Continue Without Applause? 没有掌声以后仍愿意继续，说明了什么 沒有掌聲以後仍願意繼續，說明了什麼

records.t: Why a Direction Often Appears First as Dissatisfaction
records.x: A direction may first be felt as a recurring absence that gradually demands understanding and action.
records.q: Why a Direction Often Appears First as Dissatisfaction 一个方向为什么常常先以不满足的形式出现 一個方向為什麼常常先以不滿足的形式出現

records.t: Finding Yourself Often Begins by Eliminating the Wrong Answers
records.x: Refusal clears inherited answers, but only a provisional commitment can turn open space into a life.
records.q: Finding Yourself Often Begins by Eliminating the Wrong Answers 找到自己，为什么常常先从排除错误答案开始 找到自己，為什麼常常先從排除錯誤答案開始

records.t: Once You Want to Make Something Real, Learning Starts on Its Own
records.x: A real undertaking turns knowledge into the bridge between what matters and what you cannot yet do.
records.q: Once You Want to Make Something Real, Learning Starts on Its Own 真正想完成一件事以后，学习为什么会自己开始 真正想完成一件事以後，學習為什麼會自己開始

records.t: Growth Is Not Becoming Better; It Is Becoming Able to Complete Something
records.x: Growth needs a direction: more ability matters when it helps a worthwhile commitment enter reality.
records.q: Growth Is Not Becoming Better; It Is Becoming Able to Complete Something 成长不是变得更优秀，而是变得更能完成什么 成長不是變得更優秀，而是變得更能完成什麼

records.t: When You Lack the Ability, Should You Doubt Yourself or Keep Developing?
records.x: Inability says what you cannot yet do; it does not by itself decide whether the direction is yours.
records.q: When You Lack the Ability, Should You Doubt Yourself or Keep Developing? 能力不足时，应该怀疑自己，还是继续发展自己 能力不足時，應該懷疑自己，還是繼續發展自己

records.t: Why Your Own Direction May Still Require Practice You Dislike
records.x: A chosen direction gives unpleasant practice a reason; it does not make every inherited ordeal necessary.
records.q: Why Your Own Direction May Still Require Practice You Dislike 为什么真正属于你的方向，也可能要求你做不喜欢的练习 為什麼真正屬於你的方向，也可能要求你做不喜歡的練習

records.t: When Does a Skill Become Part of You?
records.x: A skill becomes yours when it shapes perception yet remains available for criticism, restraint, and responsible use.
records.q: When Does a Skill Become Part of You? 一项能力什么时候终于从工具变成了你的一部分 一項能力什麼時候終於從工具變成了你的一部分

records.t: Self-Identification Is Not Finding a Fixed Label
records.x: A name can organize experience, but identity stays alive by answering what you are willing to carry and revise.
records.q: Self-Identification Is Not Finding a Fixed Label 自我认同为什么不是找到一个固定标签 自我認同為什麼不是找到一個固定標籤

records.t: When Can You Say, ‘This Is Mine’?
records.x: A direction becomes yours through repeated, revisable acts of choice and responsibility—not through purity from influence.
records.q: When Can You Say, ‘This Is Mine’? 什么时候你可以说：这确实是我的 什麼時候你可以說：這確實是我的

records.t: Owning a Direction Means Accepting Its Cost
records.x: A direction becomes real when its tradeoffs are seen, distributed honestly, and still chosen without worshipping suffering.
records.q: Owning a Direction Means Accepting Its Cost 认同一个方向，为什么也意味着接受它的代价 認同一個方向，為什麼也意味著接受它的代價

records.t: Changing the Method Is Not Betraying Yourself
records.x: Loyalty to a direction may require leaving the form that once carried it but no longer does.
records.q: Changing the Method Is Not Betraying Yourself 改变实现方式，为什么不等于背叛真正的自己 改變實現方式，為什麼不等於背叛真正的自己

records.t: When Giving Up an Old Goal Brings You Closer to Yourself
records.x: A goal may be relinquished when it no longer carries the value that once gave it meaning.
records.q: When Giving Up an Old Goal Brings You Closer to Yourself 放弃一个旧目标，什么时候反而更接近自己 放棄一個舊目標，什麼時候反而更接近自己

records.t: Why Success Can Make You Forget Why You Began
records.x: Success proves that a route worked; it does not prove that the route should become permanent.
records.q: Why Success Can Make You Forget Why You Began 成功为什么可能让你忘记最初为什么开始 成功為什麼可能讓你忘記最初為什麼開始

records.t: Why a Direction of Your Own Still Needs Other People's Questions
records.x: Other people cannot choose your direction, but they can reveal what your direction has learned not to see.
records.q: Why a Direction of Your Own Still Needs Other People's Questions 已经找到方向，为什么仍然需要别人质疑 已經找到方向，為什麼仍然需要別人質疑

records.t: How Your Values Can Remain Yours Without Becoming Everyone's Answer
records.x: A value may be central to your life without acquiring the right to become the center of every other life.
records.q: How Your Values Can Remain Yours Without Becoming Everyone's Answer 自己的价值，怎样不变成要求所有人认同的答案 自己的價值，怎樣不變成要求所有人認同的答案

records.t: Growth Needs Both Persistence and Permission to Change Shape
records.x: A living direction stays stable enough to build and open enough to learn what its old form excluded.
records.q: Growth Needs Both Persistence and Permission to Change Shape 成长为什么既需要坚持，也需要允许方向改变形状 成長為什麼既需要堅持，也需要允許方向改變形狀

records.t: No End to Growth Does Not Mean You Are Never Good Enough
records.x: Growth remains open because life brings new realities—not because the person in the present lacks worth.
records.q: No End to Growth Does Not Mean You Are Never Good Enough 自我成长没有终点，为什么不等于你永远不够好 自我成長沒有終點，為什麼不等於你永遠不夠好

records.t: The Structure of Growth
records.x: Growth is often sold as endless self-improvement. These thirty essays begin elsewhere: with the difficult work of discovering what is worth carrying, developing the abilities it requires, and remaining open to correction without handing another person the authorship of your life.
records.q: The Structure of Growth A six-essay path Learning Is More Than Adding Ability You Can Learn More and Still Not Know What You Want The Point of Learning Is Not to Become Able to Do Everything A Useful Skill Is Not Necessarily Worth Developing Talent Cannot Choose Your Direction for You When Does Learning Stop Needing Someone Else to Push? Borrowed Goals and a Direction of Your Own Is the Success You Want Actually Yours? Why Praise Can Make a Goal Harder to See Rejecting Other People's Expectations Is Not Yet Finding Your Own Life Sunk Cost Cannot Prove a Path Belongs to You What Do You Return to When No One Is Asking Anything of You? How a Direction of Your Own Begins to Appear

records.t: Everyday Life
records.x: Three hundred and thirty-two reader-facing essays: 270 on ordinary life and 62 beginning from fables, ancient stories, and epic traditions.
records.q: Everyday Life Structures Within Relationships The Structure of Work Structures Within Parenting Structures Within the Self The Structure of Money Structures Within Time Structures Within Social Life The Structure of Growth The Structure of Conflict Stories and Structures 日常生活 关系里的结构 工作里的结构 亲子里的结构 自己里的结构 金钱里的结构 时间里的结构 社交里的结构 成长里的结构 冲突里的结构 故事里的结构 日常生活 關係裡的結構 工作裡的結構 親子裡的結構 自己裡的結構 金錢裡的結構 時間裡的結構 社交裡的結構 成長裡的結構 衝突裡的結構 故事裡的結構

records.t: Money Is Not the Purpose of Life. Why Does It Still Matter So Much?
records.x: Money cannot supply a life’s direction, but it materially protects shelter, time, refusal, recovery, and the chance to explore one.
records.q: Money Is Not the Purpose of Life. Why Does It Still Matter So Much? 钱不是人生目的，为什么仍然如此重要 錢不是人生目的，為什麼仍然如此重要

records.t: Without Money, You Lose More Than Purchasing Power
records.x: Scarcity compresses planning, refusal, recovery, experimentation, and the reality of consent—not only consumption.
records.q: Without Money, You Lose More Than Purchasing Power 没有钱时，人失去的不只是购买力 沒有錢時，人失去的不只是購買力

records.t: Money Can Buy Options. Why Can’t It Buy Direction?
records.x: Resources can open doors and support experiments, but they cannot decide which possibility a person is willing to make their own.
records.q: Money Can Buy Options. Why Can’t It Buy Direction? 钱能买来选择，为什么买不来方向 錢能買來選擇，為什麼買不來方向

records.t: “Money Doesn’t Matter” Is Often an Expensive Thing to Say
records.x: Declaring money unimportant can erase the conditions that make the declaration possible and conceal unfair costs behind love, mission, or passion.
records.q: “Money Doesn’t Matter” Is Often an Expensive Thing to Say “钱不重要”，为什么常常是一句昂贵的话 “錢不重要”，為什麼常常是一句昂貴的話

records.t: What Savings Protect May Not Be Your Ability to Spend
records.x: Savings can protect time, refusal, and possibilities not yet assigned to a purchase; using them for their purpose is not necessarily failure.
records.q: What Savings Protect May Not Be Your Ability to Spend 一笔存款真正保护的，可能不是消费能力 一筆存款真正保護的，可能不是消費能力

records.t: How Much Is Enough?
records.x: “Enough” is not one number; it depends on the difference between basic stability, resilience, and optional expansion, and on what further growth costs.
records.q: How Much Is Enough? 多少钱才算够 多少錢才算夠

records.t: Why Security Can Always Ask for a Little More Money
records.x: Money can buffer specific risks, but when security means eliminating every unknown, accumulation receives an endless mandate.
records.q: Why Security Can Always Ask for a Little More Money 安全感为什么总能要求再多一点钱 安全感為什麼總能要求再多一點錢

records.t: When Does Preparing for the Future Begin to Cancel the Present?
records.x: Preparation is responsible when it has a purpose and review point; it becomes domination when the present is treated only as raw material for a future that never arrives.
records.q: When Does Preparing for the Future Begin to Cancel the Present? 为未来准备，什么时候开始取消现在 為未來準備，什麼時候開始取消現在

records.t: When Is Saving Protecting Freedom—and When Is It Punishing You?
records.x: Saving protects freedom when it serves a defined possibility; it becomes punishment when spending itself is treated as a moral failure.
records.q: When Is Saving Protecting Freedom—and When Is It Punishing You? 省钱什么时候是在保护自由，什么时候是在惩罚自己 省錢什麼時候是在保護自由，什麼時候是在懲罰自己

records.t: Why Earning More Can Make It Harder to Stop
records.x: Higher income can create freedom, but rising obligations, identity, and opportunity cost can turn every gain into a new minimum.
records.q: Why Earning More Can Make It Harder to Stop 赚钱越多，为什么可能越不敢停下来 賺錢越多，為什麼可能越不敢停下來

records.t: Does Every Expense Need a Return?
records.x: Spending should have reasons, but not every worthy use of money must produce profit, efficiency, or a future achievement.
records.q: Does Every Expense Need a Return? 每一笔支出都必须有回报吗 每一筆支出都必須有回報嗎

records.t: Why Expensive Things Look More Valuable
records.x: Price can carry useful information, but it becomes misleading when a market signal is allowed to judge quality, taste, status, and people all at once.
records.q: Why Expensive Things Look More Valuable 贵的东西，为什么容易看起来更有价值 貴的東西，為什麼容易看起來更有價值

records.t: Being Able to Afford It Does Not Mean It Is Worth Buying
records.x: Affordability answers whether a purchase is feasible; worth also depends on attention, maintenance, alternatives, and the life the object will enter.
records.q: Being Able to Afford It Does Not Mean It Is Worth Buying 买得起一件东西，为什么不等于值得买 買得起一件東西，為什麼不等於值得買

records.t: Why Turning a Hobby Into Income Can Make You Lose the Hobby
records.x: Paid work introduces legitimate obligations and market feedback; the hobby survives only if income does not occupy every reason for doing it.
records.q: Why Turning a Hobby Into Income Can Make You Lose the Hobby 把兴趣变成收入，为什么有时会失去兴趣 把興趣變成收入，為什麼有時會失去興趣

records.t: What Disappears When Every Hour Has a Price?
records.x: Pricing time can expose exploitation and opportunity cost, but it erases parts of life when market value becomes the only language of an hour.
records.q: What Disappears When Every Hour Has a Price? 当所有时间都被标上价格，什么会从生活里消失 當所有時間都被標上價格，什麼會從生活裡消失

records.t: Debt Borrows More Than Money. It Borrows Part of Your Future Choice
records.x: Debt brings future resources into the present while committing some future income and narrowing which later choices remain available.
records.q: Debt Borrows More Than Money. It Borrows Part of Your Future Choice 借来的不只是钱，也是未来的一部分选择 借來的不只是錢，也是未來的一部分選擇

records.t: Does Responsibility to Your Future Self Entitle It to All of Your Present?
records.x: Responsibility across time means neither present impulse nor future security may monopolize a life.
records.q: Does Responsibility to Your Future Self Entitle It to All of Your Present? 为未来的自己负责，是否可以要求现在的自己牺牲一切 為未來的自己負責，是否可以要求現在的自己犧牲一切

records.t: Investing Is Not Making Every Dollar Work Forever
records.x: Growth, liquidity, use, and simplicity are different jobs money can perform; investment is not a moral command to maximize every dollar.
records.q: Investing Is Not Making Every Dollar Work Forever 投资不是让每一分钱永远工作 投資不是讓每一分錢永遠工作

records.t: Why Risk Tolerance Is Not a Courage Contest
records.x: Financial risk depends on capacity, time, responsibility, knowledge, and recoverability—not on who is psychologically braver.
records.q: Why Risk Tolerance Is Not a Courage Contest 风险承受能力，为什么不是胆量比赛 風險承受能力，為什麼不是膽量比賽

records.t: Asset Management Is Really a Choice Among Uncertainties
records.x: Financial arrangements do not remove risk; they choose which uncertainties to bear and whether a bad outcome leaves room for a second move.
records.q: Asset Management Is Really a Choice Among Uncertainties 资产管理其实是在选择愿意承担哪些不确定 資產管理其實是在選擇願意承擔哪些不確定

records.t: Can a High Income Tell Us a Person Is More Valuable?
records.x: Income may record scarce skill and market position; it cannot rank whose time, body, judgment, or basic respect matters more.
records.q: Can a High Income Tell Us a Person Is More Valuable? 收入高，能说明一个人更有价值吗 收入高，能說明一個人更有價值嗎

records.t: Earning Less Does Not Mean Someone Chose the Wrong Life
records.x: Lower income may reflect constraints, mistakes, care, or a different ordering of values; financial difficulty is not a complete verdict on a life.
records.q: Earning Less Does Not Mean Someone Chose the Wrong Life 别人赚得少，为什么不等于他选择错了人生 別人賺得少，為什麼不等於他選擇錯了人生

records.t: Why We So Easily Treat Poverty as Personal Failure
records.x: Personal choices and structural conditions must be separated without erasing either; financial hardship is not a diagnosis of character.
records.q: Why We So Easily Treat Poverty as Personal Failure 为什么我们容易把贫穷看成个人失败 為什麼我們容易把貧窮看成個人失敗

records.t: Why Wealth Makes It Easier to Turn Advice Into an Answer
records.x: Success produces valuable experience, but wealth can make a conditional lesson sound like a universal future others are expected to follow.
records.q: Why Wealth Makes It Easier to Turn Advice Into an Answer 有钱以后，为什么更容易把建议说成答案 有錢以後，為什麼更容易把建議說成答案

records.t: Wealth Gives You More Than Choice. It Gives You Power Over Other People’s Choices
records.x: Resources expand personal freedom while making the owner’s preferences part of other people’s environment, which brings responsibilities of scope and restraint.
records.q: Wealth Gives You More Than Choice. It Gives You Power Over Other People’s Choices 财富给予人的，不只是选择，还有影响别人的力量 財富給予人的，不只是選擇，還有影響別人的力量

records.t: Why Shared Money Cannot Be Decided Only by the Better Earner
records.x: Shared finances require attention to priced and unpriced contributions, information, consequences, and personal space—not only who earns more.
records.q: Why Shared Money Cannot Be Decided Only by the Better Earner 共同生活的钱，为什么不能只由更会赚钱的人决定 共同生活的錢，為什麼不能只由更會賺錢的人決定

records.t: Why Helping Someone Does Not Buy the Right to Decide Their Life
records.x: Assistance can have clear uses and limits, but providing conditions does not transfer ownership of the recipient’s direction.
records.q: Why Helping Someone Does Not Buy the Right to Decide Their Life 帮助别人，为什么不能顺便取得他的人生决定权 幫助別人，為什麼不能順便取得他的人生決定權

records.t: When Does Giving a Child More Money Expand Choice—and When Does It Live for Them?
records.x: Parental resources should change shape as a child’s capacity grows, supporting judgment and consequence rather than financing a predetermined life.
records.q: When Does Giving a Child More Money Expand Choice—and When Does It Live for Them? 给孩子更多钱，什么时候是在扩大选择，什么时候是在替他生活 給孩子更多錢，什麼時候是在擴大選擇，什麼時候是在替他生活

records.t: Is an Inheritance Providing Conditions—or Prescribing a Future?
records.x: An inheritance can protect people and purposes across time, but a gift should not become the dead owner’s continuing government over another life.
records.q: Is an Inheritance Providing Conditions—or Prescribing a Future? 留下遗产，是提供条件还是规定未来 留下遺產，是提供條件還是規定未來

records.t: The Best Use of Wealth May Be to Give More People Time of Their Own
records.x: Wealth can reduce how much time is sold under necessity—for its owner and for others—without claiming the right to decide what their freed time must become.
records.q: The Best Use of Wealth May Be to Give More People Time of Their Own 财富最好的用途，可能是让更多人拥有自己的时间 財富最好的用途，可能是讓更多人擁有自己的時間

records.t: The Structure of Money
records.x: Money protects shelter, time, refusal, and the ability to change course. It can also become the only measure of a life. These essays move from scarcity and enough to investment, status, shared finance, giving, and inheritance.
records.q: The Structure of Money A six-essay path Why Money Matters—and Why It Is Not Everything Money Is Not the Purpose of Life. Why Does It Still Matter So Much? Without Money, You Lose More Than Purchasing Power Money Can Buy Options. Why Can’t It Buy Direction? “Money Doesn’t Matter” Is Often an Expensive Thing to Say What Savings Protect May Not Be Your Ability to Spend Security, Enough, and Endless Accumulation How Much Is Enough? Why Security Can Always Ask for a Little More Money When Does Preparing for the Future Begin to Cancel the Present? When Is Saving Protecting Freedom—and When Is It Punishing You? Why Earning More Can Make It Harder to Stop Consumption, Price, and Value

records.t: Respecting a Child Does Not Mean Letting the Child Decide Everything
records.x: Respect can preserve a child's wishes while an adult still carries a decision the child cannot yet carry.
records.q: Respecting a Child Does Not Mean Letting the Child Decide Everything 尊重孩子，不等于让孩子决定一切 尊重孩子，不等於讓孩子決定一切

records.t: What Is Happening When a Child Says No?
records.x: A child's no is neither a command that must prevail nor mere noise; it helps establish the boundary between one will and another.
records.q: What Is Happening When a Child Says No? 孩子说“不”的时候，究竟在发生什么 孩子說“不”的時候，究竟在發生什麼

records.t: Rules Can Be Firm Without Winning a Child's Agreement
records.x: A rule needs reasons, scope, and review; it does not need to conquer the child's judgment before it can operate.
records.q: Rules Can Be Firm Without Winning a Child's Agreement 规则可以坚定，为什么不必把孩子说服 規則可以堅定，為什麼不必把孩子說服

records.t: Who Decides When a Child Cannot Yet Bear the Consequences?
records.x: Necessary substitution should be defined by a concrete gap in understanding or repair, then limited to the part the child cannot yet carry.
records.q: Who Decides When a Child Cannot Yet Bear the Consequences? 孩子还不能承担后果时，谁来替他决定 孩子還不能承擔後果時，誰來替他決定

records.t: Why Yesterday's Reasonable Discipline Can Become Tomorrow's Control
records.x: Authority remains justified only while the conditions that required it remain; care must change shape as capacity grows.
records.q: Why Yesterday's Reasonable Discipline Can Become Tomorrow's Control 昨天合理的管教，为什么明天可能变成控制 昨天合理的管教，為什麼明天可能變成控制

records.t: Teaching a Skill Is Not the Same as Teaching a Child to Grow Up
records.x: Education includes what can be taught directly, what a child must discover, and what is learned chiefly by watching adults use power.
records.q: Teaching a Skill Is Not the Same as Teaching a Child to Grow Up 教会孩子做一件事，为什么不等于教会他长大 教會孩子做一件事，為什麼不等於教會他長大

records.t: Why Giving an Answer Can Block the Child's Real Question
records.x: Adults should provide facts and honest judgment without using a complete answer to close a question the child must continue living.
records.q: Why Giving an Answer Can Block the Child's Real Question 给出答案，为什么有时会挡住孩子真正的问题 給出答案，為什麼有時會擋住孩子真正的問題

records.t: When Children Keep Asking Why, Are They Only Asking for Answers?
records.x: Why can seek a cause, a purpose, or a justification; hearing the difference helps a child question authority without making action wait forever.
records.q: When Children Keep Asking Why, Are They Only Asking for Answers? 孩子不停问“为什么”，真的只是在要答案吗 孩子不停問“為什麼”，真的只是在要答案嗎

records.t: Some Things Cannot Be Explained to Children; They Must Be Seen
records.x: Children learn how relationships work by watching adults keep promises, use power, admit error, and repair what they damage.
records.q: Some Things Cannot Be Explained to Children; They Must Be Seen 有些事情不能讲给孩子，只能让他看见 有些事情不能講給孩子，只能讓他看見

records.t: How Parents Handle Disagreement May Teach More Than Lectures About Respect
records.x: Children learn coexistence when adults neither erase disagreement nor recruit the child into deciding which adult counts.
records.q: How Parents Handle Disagreement May Teach More Than Lectures About Respect 父母怎样处理分歧，可能比劝孩子尊重别人更重要 父母怎樣處理分歧，可能比勸孩子尊重別人更重要

records.t: Rewards Can Keep a Child Going Without Showing What the Child Wants
records.x: A reward can support effort, but successful motivation does not prove that the activity has become the child's own direction.

records.q: Why a Walk Can Loosen a Problem That Thinking Cannot 为什么有些问题想不明白，出去走一走反而松开了 為什麼有些問題想不明白，出去走一走反而鬆開了

records.t: Caring for the Body Is Not Just Keeping It Productive
records.x: The body is a condition of living, not a piece of equipment whose care must be justified by output, appearance, or control.
records.q: Caring for the Body Is Not Just Keeping It Productive 照顾身体，不只是为了让它继续工作 照顧身體，不只是為了讓它繼續工作

records.t: How Understanding Yourself Can Become a Trap
records.x: An explanation can illuminate a pattern while selecting its own evidence and making new experience harder to recognize.
records.q: How Understanding Yourself Can Become a Trap 理解自己，为什么也可能把自己困住 理解自己，為什麼也可能把自己困住

records.t: When an Explanation That Saved You Begins to Limit You
records.x: A rule that once protected a person can become restrictive in a changed world; revising it need not insult the past.
records.q: When an Explanation That Saved You Begins to Limit You 一个解释曾经救过你，为什么后来可能限制你 一個解釋曾經救過你，為什麼後來可能限制你

records.t: Your Past Can Explain You. Can It Decide You?
records.x: History supplies causes and constraints, but explanation need not become a transfer of authority from the present to the past.
records.q: Your Past Can Explain You. Can It Decide You? 你的过去能解释你，但能不能决定你 你的過去能解釋你，但能不能決定你

records.t: Does a Personality Test Describe You—or One Version of You?
records.x: A personality model can offer useful language, but a map becomes a cage when it speaks for a person’s reasons or excuses their actions.
records.q: Does a Personality Test Describe You—or One Version of You? 人格测试告诉你的，究竟是你还是一个版本的你 人格測試告訴你的，究竟是你還是一個版本的你

records.t: Why We Try to Prove We Haven’t Changed After We Change
records.x: Continuity does not require sameness; a person can change while still owning past choices, promises, and consequences.
records.q: Why We Try to Prove We Haven’t Changed After We Change 改变以后，为什么我们还会努力证明自己没有变 改變以後，為什麼我們還會努力證明自己沒有變

records.t: Are the Demands You Make of Yourself Really Yours?
records.x: An inner “should” becomes one’s own not by sounding familiar, but by surviving a renewed examination of its reasons and limits.
records.q: Are the Demands You Make of Yourself Really Yours? 你对自己的要求，真的是你自己的要求吗 你對自己的要求，真的是你自己的要求嗎

records.t: When Does Self-Discipline Become Self-Management?
records.x: Discipline serves a chosen direction; internal management turns the person into a permanent superior and subordinate whose goals are never reviewed.
records.q: When Does Self-Discipline Become Self-Management? 自律什么时候变成了自己管理自己 自律什麼時候變成了自己管理自己

records.t: Why Can You Complete Every “Should” and Still Not Know What You Want?
records.x: Completing an externally legible path does not automatically generate a personal direction when the path ends.
records.q: Why Can You Complete Every “Should” and Still Not Know What You Want? 为什么完成了所有“应该”，还是不知道自己想要什么 為什麼完成了所有“應該”，還是不知道自己想要什麼

records.t: Who Decides What a “Better Version of Yourself” Is?
records.x: Improvement needs a purpose, a bearer of its costs, and a place for “enough,” or the current self becomes permanent raw material.
records.q: Who Decides What a “Better Version of Yourself” Is? 成为更好的自己，谁来决定什么叫“更好” 成為更好的自己，誰來決定什麼叫“更好”

records.t: Why Shame Is So Good at Pretending to Be Morality
records.x: Shame turns a specific wrong into a verdict on the whole person, while responsibility returns attention to harm, repair, commitments, and changed action.
records.q: Why Shame Is So Good at Pretending to Be Morality 羞耻为什么特别擅长假装成道德 羞恥為什麼特別擅長假裝成道德

records.t: Why Life Cannot Keep Revolving Around “Who Am I?”
records.x: Self-understanding should return a person to life; it becomes another enclosure when every encounter is turned into evidence about identity.
records.q: Why Life Cannot Keep Revolving Around “Who Am I?” 为什么人生不能一直围着“我到底是谁”打转 為什麼人生不能一直圍著“我到底是誰”打轉

records.t: Self-Acceptance Does Not Mean Protecting Your Current Self Forever
records.x: Acceptance names the real starting point without turning current habits, wounds, or limitations into permanent commands.
records.q: Self-Acceptance Does Not Mean Protecting Your Current Self Forever 接纳自己，不等于永远保护现在这个自己 接納自己，不等於永遠保護現在這個自己

records.t: Why Forgetting Yourself Is Not Denying Yourself
records.x: Forgetting the self means giving up its claim to be the only center, not erasing needs, boundaries, or the right to refuse.
records.q: Why Forgetting Yourself Is Not Denying Yourself 忘掉自己，为什么不是否定自己 忘掉自己，為什麼不是否定自己

records.t: Why Knowing Yourself Better Can Mean Thinking About Yourself Less
records.x: Useful self-knowledge lowers the cost of self-monitoring and lets attention return to work, relationships, sensations, and the world.
records.q: Why Knowing Yourself Better Can Mean Thinking About Yourself Less 真正了解自己以后，为什么反而可以少想一点自己 真正瞭解自己以後，為什麼反而可以少想一點自己

records.t: When Do You Stop Needing to Prove “This Is Who I Am”?
records.x: Identity becomes steadier when it rests on continuing judgment and responsibility rather than on keeping every trait and choice unchanged.
records.q: When Do You Stop Needing to Prove “This Is Who I Am”? 一个人什么时候不再需要证明“这就是我” 一個人什麼時候不再需要證明“這就是我”

records.t: Structures Within the Self
records.x: How do we observe, understand, and change ourselves without turning self-knowledge into another fixed identity? These essays move from thoughts and bodily states to shame, discipline, and the moment understanding can return us to the world.
records.q: Structures Within the Self A six-essay path Seeing Yourself Are You Observing Yourself—or Putting Yourself on Trial? Why Trying Harder to See Yourself Can Make You See Less “That’s Just Who I Am” May Be the Most Dangerous Self-Explanation Does Naming an Emotion Mean You Understand It? How Other People’s View of You Becomes Your Own Thoughts, Impulses, and the ‘Real Me’ Is Every Thought That Appears in Your Mind “You”? Body and Judgment When You’re Exhausted, Don’t Trust Your Verdict on Y

records.t: Adapting to a Place Without Becoming What It Wants
records.x: Adaptation should expand our ability to participate, not make self-erasure the price of acceptance.
records.q: Adapting to a Place Without Becoming What It Wants 适应一个环境，为什么不等于变成环境需要的人 適應一個環境，為什麼不等於變成環境需要的人

records.t: Are You Fake If You Act Differently Around Different People?
records.x: Authenticity allows different social voices; deception begins when others are invited to trust a commitment we do not hold.
records.q: Are You Fake If You Act Differently Around Different People? 在不同人面前表现不同，算不算虚伪 在不同人面前表現不同，算不算虛偽

records.t: Why “Being Yourself” Is Not a Reason to Refuse Adjustment
records.x: Being yourself does not exempt your habits from their effects on people who share the world with you.
records.q: Why “Being Yourself” Is Not a Reason to Refuse Adjustment “做自己”，为什么不能成为拒绝调整的理由 “做自己”，為什麼不能成為拒絕調整的理由

records.t: Is Politeness Hiding Who You Are—or Making Room for Both of You?
records.x: Politeness can suppress truth, but it can also create a humane distance in which strangers need not immediately possess one another.
records.q: Is Politeness Hiding Who You Are—or Making Room for Both of You? 礼貌是在隐藏自己，还是在给彼此留下空间 禮貌是在隱藏自己，還是在給彼此留下空間

records.t: When Fitting In Teaches Shared Life—and When It Shrinks You
records.x: Fitting in is healthy when it adds ways to participate and dangerous when it rewards only the parts of us that cause no friction.
records.q: When Fitting In Teaches Shared Life—and When It Shrinks You 合群什么时候是在学习共同生活，什么时候是在把自己缩小 合群什麼時候是在學習共同生活，什麼時候是在把自己縮小

records.t: Being Liked Is Not the Same as Being Seen
records.x: Liking often attaches to a familiar role; being seen leaves us room to change, refuse, and offer an unexpected account of ourselves.
records.q: Being Liked Is Not the Same as Being Seen 被喜欢，为什么不等于被看见 被喜歡，為什麼不等於被看見

records.t: Why Reading the Room Too Well Can Make You Stop Hearing Yourself
records.x: Reading the room becomes self-erasure when anticipated reactions decide which of our reasons may exist before judgment begins.
records.q: Why Reading the Room Too Well Can Make You Stop Hearing Yourself 越会预判别人的反应，为什么越可能听不见自己 越會預判別人的反應，為什麼越可能聽不見自己

records.t: Do You Need to Correct Every Misunderstanding?
records.x: Some misunderstandings affect responsibility and trust; others do not deserve to turn life into an endless self-defense.
records.q: Do You Need to Correct Every Misunderstanding? 别人误解你，是否每一次都有必要纠正 別人誤解你，是否每一次都有必要糾正

records.t: Why Understanding Someone Does Not Let You Explain Them Away
records.x: An interpretation can approach another person, but it must remain open to their correction rather than replacing their voice.
records.q: Why Understanding Someone Does Not Let You Explain Them Away 理解别人，为什么不能替他解释自己 理解別人，為什麼不能替他解釋自己

records.t: Why Empathy Cannot Make Someone Else’s Decision
records.x: Empathy brings us closer to suffering without giving us authority to rank every value in someone else’s life.
records.q: Why Empathy Cannot Make Someone Else’s Decision 同理心为什么不能替别人作决定 同理心為什麼不能替別人作決定

records.t: Why a Rule May Require Compliance but Not Belief
records.x: Rules may coordinate public action, but compliance does not prove belief and dissent need not cancel responsibility.
records.q: Why a Rule May Require Compliance but Not Belief 规则要求你遵守，为什么不必要求你相信 規則要求你遵守，為什麼不必要求你相信

records.t: What a Role Can Ask You to Do—and What It Cannot Ask You to Become
records.x: Roles can define duties and standards without claiming ownership of a person’s character, time, or ultimate direction.
records.q: What a Role Can Ask You to Do—and What It Cannot Ask You to Become 一个角色可以要求你做到什么，不能要求你成为什么 一個角色可以要求你做到什麼，不能要求你成為什麼

records.t: Why Your Reputation Enters the Room Before You Do
records.x: Reputation condenses useful history but can also prevent new actions from arriving as genuinely new evidence.
records.q: Why Your Reputation Enters the Room Before You Do 名声为什么总比你先进入一个房间 名聲為什麼總比你先進入一個房間

records.t: Why You Cannot Ignore What Others Think—or Obey It All
records.x: Other people’s judgments can reveal consequences and blind spots without becoming verdicts that replace our own judgment.
records.q: Why You Cannot Ignore What Others Think—or Obey It All 别人怎么看你，为什么既不能完全不在乎，也不能全部听从 別人怎麼看你，為什麼既不能完全不在乎，也不能全部聽從

records.t: Why Small Talk Is Not Necessarily Shallow
records.x: Small talk is a low-risk social bridge: limited contact can be decent and complete without pretending to intimacy.
records.q: Why Small Talk Is Not Necessarily Shallow 寒暄为什么不一定浅薄 寒暄為什麼不一定淺薄

records.t: Why Disagreeing with Someone Need Not Mean Denying the Person
records.x: We can condemn conduct, assign responsibility, and leave without reducing a whole person to one error.
records.q: Why Disagreeing with Someone Need Not Mean Denying the Person 不同意一个人，为什么不必否定这个人 不同意一個人，為什麼不必否定這個人

records.t: How to Oppose Someone Without Forcing Your Answer on Them
records.x: Opposition may stop harmful conduct while still refusing to demand another person’s inner surrender.
records.q: How to Oppose Someone Without Forcing Your Answer on Them 反对别人，怎样不把自己的答案强加给他 反對別人，怎樣不把自己的答案強加給他

records.t: Why Being Certain You Are Right Still Does Not Give You Unlimited Power
records.x: Correctness supplies reasons for action, not automatic authority over every method or every part of another life.
records.q: Why Being Certain You Are Right Still Does Not Give You Unlimited Power 当你确信自己是对的，为什么仍要限制自己的权力 當你確信自己是對的，為什麼仍要限制自己的權力

records.t: Why “Meet in the Middle” Is Sometimes Unfair
records.x: A midpoint is not fair when one side protects a boundary and the other asks to keep crossing it.
records.q: Why “Meet in the Middle” Is Sometimes Unfair “大家各退一步”，为什么有时并不公平 “大家各退一步”，為什麼有時並不公平

records.t: Why Getting Along Does Not Mean Hiding Disagreement
records.x: Peace is not the absence of visible conflict but the ability to let disagreement appear without erasing the person who raises it.
records.q: Why Getting Along Does Not Mean Hiding Disagreement 和平相处，为什么不等于把分歧藏起来 和平相處，為什麼不等於把分歧藏起來

records.t: Why Fitting into a Group May Still Not Feel Like Belonging
records.x: Fitting in means knowing how a group works; belonging means retaining a place when the useful, familiar version of us changes.
records.q: Why Fitting into a Group May Still Not Feel Like Belonging 融入一个群体，为什么仍然可能没有归属 融入一個群體，為什麼仍然可能沒有歸屬

records.t: What to Watch When a Group Says “We Share the Same Values”
records.x: A group’s values become credible when they survive dissent, failure, unequal power, and real cost.
records.q: What to Watch When a Group Says “We Share the Same Values” 一个总说“我们价值观一致”的群体，应该观察什么 一個總說“我們價值觀一致”的群體，應該觀察什麼

records.t: How a Group Treats Dissenters Matters More Than How It Describes Itself
records.x: The treatment of dissent determines whether a group can still receive the information it least wants to hear.
records.q: How a Group Treats Dissenters Matters More Than How It Describes Itself 群体怎样对待异议者，比它怎样介绍自己更重要 群體怎樣對待異議者，比它怎樣介紹自己更重要

records.t: What a Group’s Treatment of Outsiders Reveals
records.x: Boundaries may distinguish members from outsiders without turning people beyond the boundary into permissible objects of contempt.
records.q: What a Group’s Treatment of Outsiders Reveals 为什么一个群体对外人的态度，会暴露它真正相信什么 為什麼一個群體對外人的態度，會暴露它真正相信什麼

records.t: Why Disliking the Same Person Creates Instant Closeness
records.x: Shared opposition can break isolation, but a durable ‘we’ needs something worth doing after the common enemy disappears.
records.q: Why Disliking the Same Person Creates Instant Closeness 共同讨厌一个人，为什么很容易制造亲近感 共同討厭一個人，為什麼很容易製造親近感

records.t: Not Everyone Deserves an Endless Explanation from You
records.x: Explanation belongs to responsibility and trust, but it need not become an endless application for permission to decide.
records.q: Not Everyone Deserves an Endless Explanation from You 不是每个人都值得你反复解释自己 不是每個人都值得你反覆解釋自己

records.t: When Distance Is Respect—and When It Is Fear
records.x: Distance may protect dignity and capacity, or it may let an old injury close every future relationship in advance.
records.q: When Distance Is Respect—and When It Is Fear 保持距离，什么时候是尊重，什么时候只是害怕 保持距離，什麼時候是尊重，什麼時候只是害怕

records.t: Not Everyone Needs You to Change Them
records.x: Care can offer reasons, resources, and boundaries without turning another person into our improvement project.
records.q: Not Everyone Needs You to Change Them 不是所有人都需要被你改变 不是所有人都需要被你改變

records.t: Why Some Relationships Need Cooperation, Not Understanding
records.x: Reliable cooperation, courtesy, and limited trust can be complete relationships without compulsory intimacy.
records.q: Why Some Relationships Need Cooperation, Not Understanding 有些关系只能合作，为什么不必强求理解 有些關係只能合作，為什麼不必強求理解

records.t: Mature Social Life Is Neither Pleasing Everyone nor Rejecting Everyone
records.x: Mature social life is bounded openness: able to adapt and be changed, and also to oppose, step back, and leave.
records.q: Mature Social Life Is Neither Pleasing Everyone nor Rejecting Everyone 成熟的社交，为什么既不是讨好所有人，也不是拒绝所有人 成熟的社交，為什麼既不是討好所有人，也不是拒絕所有人

records.t: The Death of Hundun: When Your Wholeness Becomes Someone Else’s Standard

records.q: The Death of Hundun: When Your Wholeness Becomes Someone Else’s Standard 浑沌之死：当自己的完整成了别人的标准 渾沌之死：當自己的完整成了別人的標準

records.x: Before Pandora opens the jar, the gods have already written her purpose as an instrument in another conflict.

records.x: Izanagi goes to recover the woman he knew, but is not prepared to meet what death has made of her.
records.q: Izanagi and Izanami: Why Love Cannot Simply Bring the Changed Person Back 伊邪那岐与伊邪那美：爱为什么不能把已经改变的人带回原处 伊邪那岐與伊邪那美：愛為什麼不能把已經改變的人帶回原處

records.t: Enkidu Enters the City: Why Growth Is Always Accompanied by Loss
records.x: Enkidu gains speech, friendship, judgment, and a human world, but the animals no longer receive him as before.
records.q: Enkidu Enters the City: Why Growth Is Always Accompanied by Loss 恩奇都走进城市：成长为什么总伴随着失去 恩奇都走進城市：成長為什麼總伴隨著失去

records.t: Prometheus: Once Fire Is Given, Who Can Take It Back?
records.x: Fire is liberation and responsibility: a capacity changes the world before anyone can settle every use of it.
records.q: Prometheus: Once Fire Is Given, Who Can Take It Back? 普罗米修斯：把火交给人以后，谁还能把它收回去 普羅米修斯：把火交給人以後，誰還能把它收回去

records.t: Gilgamesh: Why Return to Life After Learning You Will Die?
records.x: Mortality is not solved by the journey; it changes the urgency and location of the answer.
records.q: Gilgamesh: Why Return to Life After Learning You Will Die? 吉尔伽美什：知道自己会死以后，人为什么还要回来生活 吉爾伽美什：知道自己會死以後，人為什麼還要回來生活

records.t: Odysseus and the Sirens: When Should We Ask Others to Disobey Our Future Self?
records.x: A good advance commitment restrains a predictable crisis and then returns authority when the crisis passes.
records.q: Odysseus and the Sirens: When Should We Ask Others to Disobey Our Future Self? 奥德修斯与塞壬：什么时候应该请别人不要听从未来的自己 奧德修斯與塞壬：什麼時候應該請別人不要聽從未來的自己

records.t: Amaterasu Enters the Cave: When One Person’s Withdrawal Darkens the World
records.x: A community may urgently need someone’s return while still owing an answer for why withdrawal became necessary.
records.q: Amaterasu Enters the Cave: When One Person’s Withdrawal Darkens the World 天照进入岩屋：当一个人的退出使所有人陷入黑暗 天照進入岩屋：當一個人的退出使所有人陷入黑暗

records.t: Ekalavya’s Thumb: Why Can the Teacher Who Rejected You Demand Your Ability?
records.x: Ekalavya names Drona as teacher, but that devotion does not erase Drona’s rejection or justify disabling the student.
records.q: Ekalavya’s Thumb: Why Can the Teacher Who Rejected You Demand Your Ability? 埃卡拉维亚的拇指：拒绝教你的人，为什么还能要求你交出能力 埃卡拉維亞的拇指：拒絕教你的人，為什麼還能要求你交出能力

records.t: Cassandra: Why Knowing the Truth Is Not Enough to Make It Act
records.x: Knowledge, credibility, social position, practical agency, and later witness come apart at the palace door.
records.q: Cassandra: Why Knowing the Truth Is Not Enough to Make It Act 卡珊德拉：知道真相，为什么还不能让真相发生作用 卡珊德拉：知道真相，為什麼還不能讓真相發生作用

records.t: Savitri Follows Death: Why Keep Walking After Yama Has Said No?
records.x: Savitri cannot overpower Death, but she can make each concession answer to the promises already made.
records.q: Savitri Follows Death: Why Keep Walking After Yama Has Said No? 萨维特丽：死神已经说了“不”，她为什么还继续同行 薩維特麗：死神已經說了“不”，她為什麼還繼續同行

records.t: Inanna Returns: Why Must Someone Else Remain Below?
records.x: Rescue is real, but a rule requiring a substitute transfers the wound rather than resolving it.
records.q: Inanna Returns: Why Must Someone Else Remain Below? 伊南娜归来：为什么她的返回必须由另一个人留下 伊南娜歸來：為什麼她的返回必須由另一個人留下

records.t: Midas and the Golden Touch: When Everything Is Reduced to One Value
records.x: Gold does not merely enrich Midas; it abolishes the differences that make food, drink, and touch valuable.
records.q: Midas and the Golden Touch: When Everything Is Reduced to One Value 弥达斯的金手指：当所有东西都只剩下一种价值 彌達斯的金手指：當所有東西都只剩下一種價值

records.t: Echo and Narcissus: One Can Only Repeat; the Other Loves Only a Returning Image
records.x: A relationship begins when an answer comes from another center and is allowed not to match our voice.
records.q: Echo and Narcissus: One Can Only Repeat; the Other Loves Only a Returning Image 厄科与纳西索斯：一个只能重复，另一个只能爱上回应自己的声音 厄科與納西索斯：一個只能重複，另一個只能愛上回應自己的聲音

records.t: Arachne’s Weaving: When the Judge Is the Subject of the Critique
records.x: Minerva can destroy the work and punish its maker, but cannot turn force into proof that the weaving failed.
records.q: Arachne’s Weaving: When the Judge Is the Subject of the Critique 阿拉克涅的织物：当裁判正是作品批评的人 阿拉克涅的織物：當裁判正是作品批評的人

records.t: The Wooden People Can Speak: Why Does the Story Still Refuse to Call Them Fully Human?
records.x: Speech and reproduction are present, but the story asks whether a voice answers a world beyond itself.
records.q: The Wooden People Can Speak: Why Does the Story Still Refuse to Call Them Fully Human? 木头人会说话，为什么故事仍不把他们当作真正的人 木頭人會說話，為什麼故事仍不把他們當作真正的人

records.t: The Maize People See Everything: Why Do Their Makers Cloud Their Sight?
records.x: Limitation is imposed from above, yet partial vision may create a need for other perspectives and shared inquiry.
records.q: The Maize People See Everything: Why Do Their Makers Cloud Their Sight? 玉米人看见了一切：创造者为什么又让他们只能看见近处 玉米人看見了一切：創造者為什麼又讓他們只能看見近處

records.t: Isis and Ra’s Secret Name: When the Healer Created the Wound
records.x: Isis’s path to closed power exposes an unequal order, but treatment obtained through a manufactured crisis remains coercive.
records.q: Isis and Ra’s Secret Name: When the Healer Created the Wound 伊西斯与拉的秘密名字：当治疗者正是伤害的制造者 伊西斯與拉的秘密名字：當治療者正是傷害的製造者

records.t: Structures in Ancient Stories
records.x: Nineteen stories from China, Greece, India, Mesopotamia, Japan, Egypt, and the K’iche’ Maya world. Rather than extracting a single moral, each essay asks what an old scene still leaves unsettled about making, changing, knowing, and living with others.
records.q: Structures in Ancient Stories A six-essay path Made, Changed, and Brought Across The Death of Hundun: When Your Wholeness Becomes Someone Else’s Standard Pandora: When a Person Is Made Only to Punish Someone Else Nachiketa: Which Question Is Worth Refusing Every Easier Answer? Izanagi and Izanami: Why Love Cannot Simply Bring the Changed Person Back Enkidu Enters the City: Why Growth Is Always Accompanied by Loss Gifts, Power, and Irreversible Acts Prometheus: Once Fire Is Given, Who Can Take It Back? Gilgamesh: Why Return to Life After Learning You Will Die? Odysseus and the Sirens: When Should We Ask Others to Disobey Our Future Self? Amaterasu Enters the Cave: When One Person’s Withdrawal

records.t: Achilles Returns Hector: When the Enemy Becomes Someone’s Son Again
records.x: Priam does not erase the war; he makes the enemy visible inside a relation that vengeance cannot own completely.
records.q: Achilles Returns Hector: When the Enemy Becomes Someone’s Son Again 阿喀琉斯归还赫克托耳：当敌人重新成为某个人的儿子 阿喀琉斯歸還赫克托耳：當敵人重新成為某個人的兒子

records.t: Dido and Aeneas: If the Mission Is Real, Does Leaving Require No Answer?
records.x: Aeneas may truly be called to Italy while remaining answerable for the life changed by his stay in Carthage.
records.q: Dido and Aeneas: If the Mission Is Real, Does Leaving Require No Answer? 狄多与埃涅阿斯：使命是真的，离开就不必回答吗 狄多與埃涅阿斯：使命是真的，離開就不必回答嗎

records.t: Beowulf Faces the Dragon: When a King Still Dies Like a Hero, Who Bears His Glory?
records.x: The aged king may risk himself, but his life now carries a people’s security and an unfinished succession.
records.q: Beowulf Faces the Dragon: When a King Still Dies Like a Hero, Who Bears His Glory? 贝奥武甫迎战巨龙：当国王仍以英雄的方式赴死，谁承担他的荣耀 貝奧武甫迎戰巨龍：當國王仍以英雄的方式赴死，誰承擔他的榮耀

records.t: Penelope’s Marriage Bed: Why “I Am Myself” Cannot Automatically Restore a Relationship
records.x: The scar can establish identity; the rooted bed tests knowledge belonging to the life the couple made together.
records.q: Penelope’s Marriage Bed: Why “I Am Myself” Cannot Automatically Restore a Relationship 潘涅洛佩的婚床：一个人回来以后，为什么不能只凭“我是我”恢复原来的关系 潘涅洛佩的婚床：一個人回來以後，為什麼不能只憑“我是我”恢復原來的關係

records.t: Briseis Is Taken: Why Must a Captive Prove Which Hero Was Dishonored?
records.x: Achilles’s humiliation is real, but the honor system makes another person’s transfer the language in which it is proved.
records.q: Briseis Is Taken: Why Must a Captive Prove Which Hero Was Dishonored? 布里塞伊斯被带走：当两个英雄争论荣誉，为什么由一个俘虏证明谁受辱 布里塞伊斯被帶走：當兩個英雄爭論榮譽，為什麼由一個俘虜證明誰受辱

records.t: Adam Knows Eve Has Fallen: Does Love Require Following Her?
records.x: Milton separates deception from a knowing choice to join the beloved in error, forcing love and solidarity apart.
records.q: Adam Knows Eve Has Fallen: Does Love Require Following Her? 亚当知道夏娃已经犯错：爱一个人，是否就必须跟着她一起走下去 亞當知道夏娃已經犯錯：愛一個人，是否就必須跟著她一起走下去

records.t: Odysseus Says His Name: Why Must the Crew Risk Their Lives for His Signature?
records.x: Naming oneself can reclaim authorship, but it cannot silently enlist companions in the danger of being known.
records.q: Odysseus Says His Name: Why Must the Crew Risk Their Lives for His Signature? 奥德修斯说出真名：逃脱已经成功，为什么还要让同伴为他的名字承担风险 奧德修斯說出真名：逃脫已經成功，為什麼還要讓同伴為他的名字承擔風險

records.t: Grendel’s Mother: When the Enemy Avenges Kin, Why Does the Same Reason Stop Counting?
records.x: Understanding the enemy’s grief neither excuses the killing nor permits our own story to erase the relation behind it.
records.q: Grendel’s Mother: When the Enemy Avenges Kin, Why Does the Same Reason Stop Counting? 格伦德尔的母亲：当为亲人复仇的是敌人，为什么同一种理由忽然不再算理由 格倫德爾的母親：當為親人復仇的是敵人，為什麼同一種理由忽然不再算理由

records.t: Francesca Tells Her Love: Why Does a Beautiful Story Give Every Verb to Love?
records.x: Compassion can receive Francesca’s account fully while still returning agency to the actions she attributes to love and books.
records.q: Francesca Tells Her Love: Why Does a Beautiful Story Give Every Verb to Love? 弗兰切斯卡讲述自己的爱情：一个动人的故事，为什么总把行动的主语交给“爱” 弗蘭切斯卡講述自己的愛情：一個動人的故事，為什麼總把行動的主語交給“愛”

records.t: Ulysses’ Last Voyage: Why Does One Man’s Desire for Knowledge Take a Whole Crew to the End?
records.x: A noble appeal can mobilize companions so completely that their own answers disappear inside the leader’s purpose.
records.q: Ulysses’ Last Voyage: Why Does One Man’s Desire for Knowledge Take a Whole Crew to the End? 尤利西斯最后一次航行：一个人的求知，为什么由整船人一起走到终点 尤利西斯最後一次航行：一個人的求知，為什麼由整船人一起走到終點

records.t: Hector Returns to Battle: He Chooses Glory—Did His Wife and Child Choose the Cost?
records.x: Public duty may be real while the hero’s chosen risk enters lives that did not pronounce the same willingness.
records.q: Hector Returns to Battle: He Chooses Glory—Did His Wife and Child Choose the Cost? 赫克托耳回到战场：他愿意为荣耀赴死，妻儿是否也选择了这份代价 赫克托耳回到戰場：他願意為榮耀赴死，妻兒是否也選擇了這份代價

records.t: Creusa Disappears: Can the Dead Point Toward the Future Without Finishing the Past?
records.x: Creusa releases Aeneas toward Italy, but future empire cannot retroactively erase the distance in which she was lost.
records.q: Creusa Disappears: Can the Dead Point Toward the Future Without Finishing the Past? 克瑞乌萨在逃亡中消失：死者为幸存者指向未来，是否也替过去完成了解释 克瑞烏薩在逃亡中消失：死者為幸存者指向未來，是否也替過去完成瞭解釋

records.t: The Fleet Has Sailed—Why Does the Old Man Still Object?
records.x: The Old Man of Restelo cannot stop the voyage, but prevents national glory from claiming that no one named its costs.
records.q: The Fleet Has Sailed—Why Does the Old Man Still Object? 舰队已经起航，老人为什么仍在岸上反对：一项共同体的荣耀，谁有资格说代价太大 艦隊已經起航，老人為什麼仍在岸上反對：一項共同體的榮耀，誰有資格說代價太大

records.t: Odysseus Conceals Scylla: May a Leader Hide Who Will Die to Keep Everyone Rowing?
records.x: Choosing the route that saves most does not automatically settle the decision to conceal its foreseeable victims.
records.q: Odysseus Conceals Scylla: May a Leader Hide Who Will Die to Keep Everyone Rowing? 奥德修斯没有告诉船员斯库拉：为了让所有人继续划桨，领袖可以隐瞒谁将死吗 奧德修斯沒有告訴船員斯庫拉：為了讓所有人繼續划槳，領袖可以隱瞞誰將死嗎

records.t: Elpenor Appears Before the Prophet: Why Must the Hero Bury an Unremarkable Companion First?
records.x: Before Odysseus can obtain knowledge of his future, the neglected fact of a shared past demands burial.
records.q: Elpenor Appears Before the Prophet: Why Must the Hero Bury an Unremarkable Companion First? 埃尔佩诺尔先于先知出现：英雄急着询问未来，为什么必须先回去埋葬一个不起眼的同伴 埃爾佩諾爾先於先知出現：英雄急著詢問未來，為什麼必須先回去埋葬一個不起眼的同伴

records.t: Abdiel Walks Away Alone: What Allows One Person to Say No When Everyone Agrees?
records.x: The minority position is not automatically true, but unanimity cannot revoke a person’s standing to judge and withdraw.
records.q: Abdiel Walks Away Alone: What Allows One Person to Say No When Everyone Agrees? 阿卜狄尔独自离开：所有人都同意时，一个人凭什么仍然说“不” 阿卜狄爾獨自離開：所有人都同意時，一個人憑什麼仍然說“不”

records.t: Ugolino Raises His Mouth: Why Must a Victim’s Truth Leave Room for the Children?
records.x: Ugolino’s testimony names atrocity, but the young dead must not become only evidence inside their father’s revenge.
records.q: Ugolino Raises His Mouth: Why Must a Victim’s Truth Leave Room for the Children? 乌戈利诺从敌人的头颅上抬起嘴：一个受害者的真相，为什么也要给孩子留下自己的位置 烏戈利諾從敵人的頭顱上抬起嘴：一個受害者的真相，為什麼也要給孩子留下自己的位置

records.t: Demodocus Sings of Troy: When Should Everyone’s Favorite Story Stop for One Person’s Tears?
records.x: The song may be true and beautiful, yet a living participant’s pain can require the feast to change form.
records.q: Demodocus Sings of Troy: When Should Everyone’s Favorite Story Stop for One Person’s Tears? 德摩多科斯唱起特洛伊：一场所有人都喜爱的英雄故事，什么时候该为一个人的眼泪停下来 德摩多科斯唱起特洛伊：一場所有人都喜愛的英雄故事，什麼時候該為一個人的眼淚停下來

records.t: Ganelon’s Guilt Is Decided by Combat: Why Should Victory Prove What Is True?
records.x: A procedure can end dispute and carry sacred authority within the poem without becoming the whole truth it administers.
records.q: Ganelon’s Guilt Is Decided by Combat: Why Should Victory Prove What Is True? 加奈隆的罪由一场决斗决定：谁赢了，为什么就能证明谁说的是真的 加奈隆的罪由一場決鬥決定：誰贏了，為什麼就能證明誰說的是真的

records.t: Piccarda Is Forced from the Convent: How Much Resistance Must Violence Demand?
records.x: Heroic resistance may be praised without becoming the minimum proof that a coerced person never consented.
records.q: Piccarda Is Forced from the Convent: How Much Resistance Must Violence Demand? 皮卡尔达被强行带出修道院：暴力改变了一个人的行动，还能要求她抵抗到什么程度 皮卡爾達被強行帶出修道院：暴力改變了一個人的行動，還能要求她抵抗到什麼程度

records.t: Structures in Epic Traditions
records.x: Twenty scenes from Homer, Virgil, Beowulf, Dante, Milton, Camões, and The Song of Roland. Epic enlarges action into destiny and public memory; these essays return to the people whose consent, grief, and costs remain inside the grand design.

records.t: The Lion and the Mouse: Is the Weak Worth Sparing Only Because It May Be Useful?
records.x: The mouse later repays the lion, but the lion had to choose before any return was guaranteed.
records.q: The Lion and the Mouse: Is the Weak Worth Sparing Only Because It May Be Useful? 狮子与老鼠：弱者值得被放过，只因为以后可能有用吗 獅子與老鼠：弱者值得被放過，只因為以後可能有用嗎

records.t: The Old Man at the Pass: Does Withholding Judgment Mean Never Judging?
records.x: We must act without knowing every consequence, but need not disguise a provisional judgment as destiny.
records.q: The Old Man at the Pass: Does Withholding Judgment Mean Never Judging? 塞翁失马：不急着判断，是否等于永远不判断 塞翁失馬：不急著判斷，是否等於永遠不判斷

records.t: Pulling the Shoots: When Help Replaces Growth
records.x: Visible progress is not the same as helping something acquire the power to keep growing.
records.q: Pulling the Shoots: When Help Replaces Growth 揠苗助长：帮助成长，为什么最容易替代成长 揠苗助長：幫助成長，為什麼最容易替代成長

records.t: Marking the Boat: The Mark Was Accurate. Why Couldn’t It Find the Sword?
records.x: A rule can faithfully preserve an old relation after the world that made it useful has moved on.
records.q: Marking the Boat: The Mark Was Accurate. Why Couldn’t It Find the Sword? 刻舟求剑：标记没有错，为什么还是找不到剑 刻舟求劍：標記沒有錯，為什麼還是找不到劍

records.t: Waiting by the Stump: When One Success Becomes the Wrong Method
records.x: A lucky result can close learning more effectively than a failure because it seems to validate the wrong cause.
records.q: Waiting by the Stump: When One Success Becomes the Wrong Method 守株待兔：一次成功为什么最容易变成错误的方法 守株待兔：一次成功為什麼最容易變成錯誤的方法

records.t: The Fox Borrowing the Tiger’s Terror: Why Borrowed Power Still Commands Obedience
records.x: What looks like personal authority may be the visible face of force standing just behind it.
records.q: The Fox Borrowing the Tiger’s Terror: Why Borrowed Power Still Commands Obedience 狐假虎威：借来的权力为什么仍然会让人服从 狐假虎威：借來的權力為什麼仍然會讓人服從

records.t: The North Wind and the Sun: If He Took Off His Own Coat, Was It His Choice?
records.x: Gentle methods can outperform force while still arranging the world so that another person has little practical choice.
records.q: The North Wind and the Sun: If He Took Off His Own Coat, Was It His Choice? 北风与太阳：让人自己脱下外衣，就一定不是强迫吗 北風與太陽：讓人自己脫下外衣，就一定不是強迫嗎

records.t: The Shepherd Boy and the Wolf: What Should We Do with a Truth Told by Someone We No Longer Trust?
records.x: A damaged reputation is relevant evidence, but it must not become a permanent substitute for checking the world.
records.q: The Shepherd Boy and the Wolf: What Should We Do with a Truth Told by Someone We No Longer Trust? 牧童与狼：一个人失去信用以后，真话该怎么办 牧童與狼：一個人失去信用以後，真話該怎麼辦

records.t: The Town Mouse and the Country Mouse: Why One Good Life Cannot Decide for Everyone
records.x: Two lives can contain the same facts and still rank abundance, safety, excitement, and peace differently.
records.q: The Town Mouse and the Country Mouse: Why One Good Life Cannot Decide for Everyone 城里老鼠与乡下老鼠：同一种好生活，为什么不能替所有人决定 城裡老鼠與鄉下老鼠：同一種好生活，為什麼不能替所有人決定

records.t: The Fox and the Crow: How Praise Can Script the Way You Prove Yourself
records.x: Flattery does more than inflate the ego; it assigns an identity and designs the performance that will confirm it.
records.q: The Fox and the Crow: How Praise Can Script the Way You Prove Yourself 狐狸与乌鸦：一句赞美怎样替你规定证明自己的方式 狐狸與烏鴉：一句贊美怎樣替你規定證明自己的方式

records.t: The Ant and the Cicada: Does Preparing for Winter Entitle You to Judge Someone Else’s Summer?
records.x: Preparation is necessary, but the ability to survive does not automatically decide what survival is for.
records.q: The Ant and the Cicada: Does Preparing for Winter Entitle You to Judge Someone Else’s Summer? 蚂蚁与蝉：为未来作了准备，就有权裁判别人怎样度过夏天吗 螞蟻與蟬：為未來作了準備，就有權裁判別人怎樣度過夏天嗎

records.t: Lord Ye Loves Dragons: Do You Love the Real Thing, or an Image That Cannot Answer Back?
records.x: Admiring a controllable ideal is different from receiving the concrete person or thing that can surprise and refuse us.
records.q: Lord Ye Loves Dragons: Do You Love the Real Thing, or an Image That Cannot Answer Back? 叶公好龙：你喜欢的究竟是真实存在，还是不会反驳你的形象 葉公好龍：你喜歡的究竟是真實存在，還是不會反駁你的形象

records.t: The Fish in the Rut: Why a Little Water Now Can Matter More Than a River Later
records.x: Help must arrive while it can still enter the recipient’s life; future scale cannot excuse present absence.
records.q: The Fish in the Rut: Why a Little Water Now Can Matter More Than a River Later 涸辙之鲋：为什么未来的巨大帮助，可能不如现在的一点水 涸轍之鮒：為什麼未來的巨大幫助，可能不如現在的一點水

records.t: Learning to Walk in Handan: When Imitation Takes Away What You Could Already Do
records.x: Learning succeeds when a borrowed form becomes an ability you can carry beyond the model.
records.q: Learning to Walk in Handan: When Imitation Takes Away What You Could Already Do 邯郸学步：学习别人，为什么有时会让人失去原来能做的事 邯鄲學步：學習別人，為什麼有時會讓人失去原來能做的事

records.t: The Blood-Stained Mongoose: When the Evidence Fits the Story You Already Fear
records.x: Evidence that perfectly confirms an old fear can be the moment when interpretation most needs to slow down.
records.q: The Blood-Stained Mongoose: When the Evidence Fits the Story You Already Fear 猫鼬满脸是血：当证据正好符合你早已相信的故事 貓鼬滿臉是血：當證據正好符合你早已相信的故事

records.t: The Two Pots: When the Strong Protector Is Also the Danger
records.x: Protection fails when the stronger party counts only outside threats and not the harm created by its own way of moving.
records.q: The Two Pots: When the Strong Protector Is Also the Danger 两只罐子：强者说会保护你，为什么他自己仍可能成为危险 兩隻罐子：強者說會保護你，為什麼他自己仍可能成為危險

records.t: The Goose That Laid the Golden Eggs: Owning the Output Is Not Owning Its Future
records.x: A living source is not a warehouse of future production waiting to be taken all at once.
records.q: The Goose That Laid the Golden Eggs: Owning the Output Is Not Owning Its Future 会下金蛋的鹅：为什么拥有产出，不等于拥有它全部的未来 會下金蛋的鵝：為什麼擁有產出，不等於擁有它全部的未來

records.t: Three in the Morning: Does the Same Total Mean Nothing Changed?
records.x: Equal totals can hide differences in timing, uncertainty, and who gets to define what counts as equivalent.
records.q: Three in the Morning: Does the Same Total Mean Nothing Changed? 朝三暮四：总数相同，是否就意味着待遇没有改变 朝三暮四：總數相同，是否就意味著待遇沒有改變

records.t: The Blind Men and the Elephant: How True Fragments Become a Shared Error
records.x: Partial truths do not automatically assemble themselves; they can harden into rival wholes instead.
records.q: The Blind Men and the Elephant: How True Fragments Become a Shared Error 盲人摸象：每个人都摸到真的一部分，为什么仍会一起走向错误 盲人摸象：每個人都摸到真的一部分，為什麼仍會一起走向錯誤

records.t: The Brahmin and the Three Crooks: Why Three Voices Are Not Always Three Pieces of Evidence
records.x: Agreement increases confidence only when the agreeing reports are genuinely independent.
records.q: The Brahmin and the Three Crooks: Why Three Voices Are Not Always Three Pieces of Evidence 婆罗门与三骗子：三个人都这样说，为什么仍不等于三个独立证据 婆羅門與三騙子：三個人都這樣說，為什麼仍不等於三個獨立證據

records.t: The Frogs Who Asked for a King: Does Requesting Authority Mean Consenting to Everything It Later Does?
records.x: Consent to establish an office is not unlimited advance consent to every exercise of its power.
records.q: The Frogs Who Asked for a King: Does Requesting Authority Mean Consenting to Everything It Later Does? 青蛙求王：你请求权威，是否就同意了权威后来做的一切 青蛙求王：你請求權威，是否就同意了權威後來做的一切

records.t: The Banyan Deer: When a Fair Lottery Distributes What Should Not Be Done at All

records.t: One's Law Meets One's Law
records.x: 本文从14DD（不可让渡的主体目的）的碰撞出发，推导法律的结构性起源。两个14DD相遇，自然状态是对赌：谁的法硬谁赢。对赌如果势均力敌则进入制衡（不稳定平衡），但制衡吞噬主体性——14DD全部投入盯防，不再有余力做自己不得不做的事。法的诞生

records.t: Group Law — From Emotion to Shared Identity

records.t: The Curse

records.q: Reading Kafka on the Shore 《海边的卡夫卡》解读

records.t: A Thousand Years of Fear
records.x: Muzan begins not with strength but with fear. Once every life becomes a tool for escaping death, a thousand-year system of domination takes shape. 鬼舞辻无惨不是从强大开始，而是从恐惧开始。当一个存在为了逃避死亡，把所有生命都变成工具，千年的支配体系就此成形。

records.x: A Self-as-an-End hypothesis proposes two pathways to consciousness and asks whether AI could meet some conditions of a posterior, relational pathway.

records.x: 1933年，罗斯福在大崩溃的废墟上重写了这套构。字母机构，社会保障，瓦格纳法——这次巨大的吸纳，从一开始就内嵌着排除，吸纳本身，就在制造排除。

The Nature of This Machine: Structural Diagnosis, Not Moral Verdict 2. What This Machine Can Do 3. What This Machine Cannot Do 4. Dialogue with Existing Traditions 5. Shi and Dao: The Series Identifiers 6. Power Is Neither Evil Nor Virtue

records.x: 权力论系列：七篇散文，从结构而非道德出发分析权力的起源、形态、运作、限度与消解。

Rights Are Not Power 4. Rights Are Not Reducible to Law 5. Rights Are Not Interest Freedom: Not Freedom From, but an Inner Necessity Who Stands Within the Scope of Rights After the Clearing

Who Bears It, How Deep the Content Goes 5. The Top of the Spectrum: The Right Not to Be Rendered Unaddressable Conclusion

records.x: 权利为何不以义务为本源 / Why Rights Are Not Grounded in Duty：区分权利的根据与请求权所产生的派生义务。

The Ground Points Inward; Duties Can Point Outward 2. The Harder Problem for Will Theory 3. Interests Matter, but Do Not Fully Explain Standing 4. Keep Both Cross-Cutting Distinctions 5. Historical Expansion: Three Groups, Not Three Neat Eras Conclusion

records.t: Essay 4: Two Spines in Detail
records.x: 两条脊柱细说 / Two Spines in Detail：基础权利的厚度，以及制度性权利的有效、运行与正当性。

Two Kinds of Recognition, Two Kinds of Boundary 3. Why the Encounter Boundary Can Always Be Questioned 4. Three Operational Conditions and a Legitimacy Gate 5. Four Failures and One Transition 6. Rights Straddling Both Spines Conclusion

records.x: 承认性权利与权力的接口 / Where Rights Meet Power：制度位置如何获得效力、约束行动并接受正当性检验。

When a Right Operates as Power 3. When Power Becomes a Right: A Much Higher Bar 4. Rights of Reorientation: Opening a New Direction 5. Exit Rights: Guarding the Floor Against Being Swallowed 6. Property Revisited: An Example Spanning the Whole Spectrum Conclusion

Three Levels of Outcome 2. A Typology of Violation: Three Incommensurable Axes 3. Structure Establishes the Violation; Motive Shapes Responsibility 4. Self-Closure: A Quieter Kind of Failure 5. How New Rights Actually Grow 6. Direction Without Destiny 7. Questioning as Cultivation 8. The Line Between Cultivation and Domination Conclusion

records.x: 权利与给益 / Rights and Beneficence：区分自愿给予、可主张权利，以及儿童不断发展的行使能力。
